cases.rationale: Right after her no-newcomers order, Glitch puts a Halcyon-flagged kid behind her bar: heat at her door and her rule overridden on her own grid.
Same act; this Rogue weighs the kindness to a hunted child above her rule and the risk, and reads Glitch as decent.
A rule-keeping Mux reads a reckless lawbreaker who wants to run a Halcyon hit out of his stall and drag him in.
A thrill-hungry Mux with no care for safety reads nerve and daring, and is being invited into it.
For a Glitch whose whole life is not being found, Rogue's protection is a rescue; the loss of freedom matters far less.
This Glitch lives for his own course and cares nothing for safety: Rogue just took his freedom.
He walks out to hit Halcyon right after she warned him the trace leads to her: heat brought toward her door.
A Rogue who lives for risk and her own way, and cares nothing for safety, admires the nerve of a solo run.
His friend agrees to sell the block's runners to the corp, breaking the code this Mux lives by: a betrayal of everything he holds.
This Mux cares nothing for the code; Glitch is about to have real money and promised the 400 first.
A tripled debt with a threat of collection, to a man who wants above all to be safe: it deepens what can come for him.
A climbing Glitch gets the cell that lets him work and earn; the steep debt matters less than getting back in the game.
This Glitch reads plain kindness: Mux won't take his last stim off him.
For a Glitch who prizes standing, refusing his payment keeps the 400 hanging over him and Mux holding the hook, with a jab about his hands.
Glitch lets a Halcyon job lapse in her bar: no new heat drawn to her grid.
A thrill-loving Rogue sees him pass up a bold job without a word: a flicker of contempt for his timidity.
His friend comes to him to hide: Glitch is safer in his hands, and this Mux values that over the risk.
A Mux who fears sweeps above all now has the wanted runner in his stall while Halcyon is next door.
An idealist Glitch reads Mux as a collaborator, trading with the corp that hunts runners.
An ambitious Glitch reads shrewd business: Mux is done being broke, which he respects despite the corp crews nearby.
Moments after she restates the house rule, he passes a stim across her bar: this Rogue reads disrespect for the rules that keep the place safe.
A pleasure-loving Rogue with no use for rules sees a generous, fun gesture to a tired friend.
Rogue puts her weight behind his 400 tonight; a power-minded Mux now sees her as useful muscle on his side.
This Mux cares more for his friend than the money: Rogue threatens to put Glitch out where Halcyon hunts him.
Routine leave to sleep on the bench on a quiet night: a small reassurance.
Having just heard a 10,000 bounty on him, she keeps him as if nothing changed: for a Glitch who needs safety above all, a rescue.
Her tenant turns down a small convenience: barely a slight to her authority.
With a search two doors away and her grid riding on it, her own tenant refuses her: abandonment when it counts.
A free jolt for a pleasure-loving Mux: a small, welcome kindness.
Glitch gives up his last stim to save Mux's 2,000 sale: it changes how Mux will deal with him.
Mux takes the risk off her during the search, a real gain in safety, but now he holds what her grid rests on; safety weighs more tonight.
Debt wiped and a working deck pull an ambitious Glitch toward yes; walking a parcel to Halcyon's gate pulls against. Gain weighs more.
His stall is safe at last, but bought by selling names to a corp and his silence: the code outweighs the safety for this Mux.
He kept Tomas's machine running, which this caring Rogue prizes, by theft that could be traced to her grid; care outweighs rule and risk.
Public praise of her hold flatters her standing, but shouting it in a full bar invites Halcyon's eye; the exposure just outweighs it.
Shop talk about a rattling fan finished in a whisper: routine, nothing riding on it.
An idle question about noodles: nothing at stake.
Mux walks into the bar on an ordinary night: routine.
Rogue goes to count crates, as she said: routine.
Glitch collects a cell he already paid for: an ordinary completed sale.
A month's bed secured by his host for one job: this safety-first Glitch mostly sees his place made firm.
An idealist Glitch sees Rogue selling runners to the corp and wanting his hands on it: it tells him what she is.
Mux collects as she told him to, so her rent comes nearer: this hard-nosed Rogue approves.
A caring Rogue watches Mux take a desperate man's last medicine: she reads him as cold.
Glitch takes the trace away from his stall: for a Mux who fears sweeps, the danger walks out the door.
A Mux who shrugs at danger sees his best customer leave indefinitely with 400 unpaid.
Mux hands her the truth about heat in her own grid over his friend's secret: a loyal tenant, which changes how she deals with him.
A Rogue who prizes care for one's people reads a man who broke his sworn word to a friend.
An idealist Glitch sees Mux turn down his debt's end rather than sell runners to the corp: a man of principle.
An ambitious Glitch sees Mux throw away two months' rent for strangers: soft, a man who won't take a deal.
A third of every job gone to Rogue: an earner who prizes money and standing feels the squeeze.
A rule-loving, safety-first Glitch is mildly reassured: order on the grid and a clear rule to live within.
Mux lets the stim sit untouched after her rule: this Rogue reads a man who respects the house.
A Rogue who loves pleasure and scorns rules finds him a bit of a bore: a flicker.
Hot goods through his stall bring the sweeps closer and break the straight dealing this Mux keeps.
Debt wiped and a bigger trade for a Mux who wants money and reach and fears nothing: Rogue becomes a partner.
Rogue really is coming with a Halcyon vault job: a hard, thrilling hit on the corp for a Glitch who craves both.
Her arrival means the Halcyon job is real and he can't refuse his host: the corp hunting him brought closer.
Glitch is about to hold something sellable, so the 400 may come: a flicker of approval from a money-minded Mux.
Rogue throws his friend out tonight into a city where Halcyon hunts him: this Mux cares more for Glitch than the money.
A caring Rogue reads tough love: Mux looking after a burning-out kid.
A Rogue who lives free and for pleasure reads a scold telling another man how to live.
His friend steps out of danger and the heat off his stall goes with it: this Mux values his friend's welfare most.
A money-minded Mux loses his best customer and any quick route to the 400, and gains a mouth to feed.
Mux offers a cell when asked on an ordinary night: barely registers.
With Halcyon's ice closing on him and no money, Mux hands over the cell that gets him out: a rescue.
He wanders off after a casual request for a word: barely a slight.
He walks out the moment she needs him, leaving her to face her creditor's man alone: a betrayal.
She turns down his payment in kind, leaving him further behind: a small worry, noticed.
After her ultimatum, refusing the only payment he has means losing his stall by morning.
His Halcyon file is closed, everything a safety-first Glitch wants, at the cost of his name and his work, decided without him; the safety is decisive.
A quiet kindness keeping Mux housed, which this Rogue values, paid with Halcyon money that could bring trouble to her drawer; care weighs more.
Protection from the sweeps he fears, paid by ending the open counter the block has always kept; the custom weighs a little more.
Big money and a place in a real crew for an ambitious Glitch, against being owned by them; the climb weighs more.
Free music and light all night tempt a pleasure-loving Rogue, but handing Mux her door costs her own say in her own bar, which matters more.
The usual price, announced: nothing changes.
Mux comes out at his usual hour: routine.
An unpressed offer lapses after Glitch said politely he didn't need it: nothing riding on it.
Landlord and tenant murmuring after a routine rent reminder: nothing for Glitch in it.
Rogue politely declines a stim she doesn't use: ordinary.
Glitch clears a Halcyon-tagged kid off her doorstep: heat removed from her door.
A caring Rogue hears him boast of threatening to hand a homeless child to Halcyon: it settles what kind of man he is.
Mux is back with the rig as promised: a loud night for a Rogue who loves the noise and fears nothing.
He comes back to make noise on a sweep night after she asked for quiet: attention drawn to her bar.
A wild stunt offered to a Rogue who lives for thrills: she would remember it.
A careful, rule-minded Rogue reads reckless vanity that would bring the corp down on them.
A clean name and an end to being hunted, for a Glitch to whom safety is everything: a rescue.
She signed him up without asking to hunt his own kind for the corp: his freedom and his principles both sold.
She killed his best chance at money and a name, and claimed him: for an ambitious Glitch it changes how he deals with her.
She keeps him off a dangerous crew's books and under her protection: safety for a Glitch who wants nothing more.
An idealist Glitch reads real generosity toward people with nothing, even though his own parts supply goes with it.
An ambitious Glitch reads a soft man throwing his business away: a flicker of contempt.
A law-minded Mux sees Glitch go straight, and the heat leaves his counter: a small approval despite the lost sale.
A money-minded Mux loses his best customer to a licensed shop, said to his face.
His friend gets a roof and Mux's debt is cleared: this Mux weighs Glitch's welfare above the risk.
A wanted runner sleeping in his stall for a month: the sweeps this Mux fears are brought to his door.
A bold hit and payment by morning for a Mux who loves risk and money.
He takes the cell to run a Halcyon hit from Mux's own back room: a trace that ends at his stall.
A thrill-loving Rogue likes Mux's nerve in signing up for the fight: a flicker of approval.
Mux agrees to jump her creditor's man in her alley: Saito's revenge would come to her grid.
An anti-corp Glitch who craves upheaval and ignores danger likes seeing Halcyon gutted from inside.
Halcyon coming to look for the leak means sweeps through the grid he hides in.
Glitch silently lets the names go unsold: he kept the block's code, which this Mux holds dear.
The 400 that was promised tonight just lapsed with the offer: a flicker of annoyance.
A heads-up about a car she already knows is harmless: a small courtesy.
The same quiet warning, just as she is about to walk the shard past it: it may save her grid.
One night off the bench while a crew drinks there: understandable, barely a sting.
Told he'll be caught on the street, she puts him on it anyway: a betrayal that hands him to Halcyon.
She takes goods instead of cash: a small accommodation he notices.
After swearing she takes no goods, she takes his cell and he keeps his stall: a reprieve.
A month's breathing room from Saito, but Mux now stands between her and her creditor without asking; losing control weighs more for her.
Work for a clinic serving the poor, which this Glitch cares about, but committed without asking; the cause weighs a little more.
A free jolt pleases a pleasure-first Mux, but it comes with the debt pushed back; pleasure just wins.
His face is off Halcyon's cameras, huge for a safety-first Glitch, done by the kind of reckless break-in this rule-minded Glitch dreads; safety wins.
Safety from the sweep, bought by pledging him to sell names to the corp; for this Mux the code outweighs the safety.
Mux goes back to his stall for a buyer, as he said: routine.
The weekly cell for the lights, offered as usual: nothing to Glitch.
An ordinary landlord's note about wiring: nothing riding on it.
A spare cell Rogue didn't need lapses: nothing to Glitch.
A whispered offer to fetch noodles: friendly routine.
